meta.order: Vol XI Part B addendum: the line-atom reduction of the cell's D(2)

LA1_scan.verdict: the line-atom family (2 parameters) attains the parity-odd family's optimum: the cell's D(2) reduces to a 2-parameter boundary problem.

LA2_reduction.statement: for the line atom the machinery degenerates to an explicit 6x6 matrix C.G with entries rational in (c, y) (block sums + the two geometric line Grams c^2/(1-y^2)^2 and c^2/(1-y^2)): ||M||^2 = the largest eigenvalue of C.G, the largest root of an explicit degree-6 polynomial
LA2_reduction.flip_symmetry: (c, y) and (-c, -y) give the same norm: the cell K is ODD under the gamma_2 parity (Pi_2 K Pi_2 = -K), so the flip (c, y) -> (-c, -y) conjugates the error
LA2_reduction.verdict: PASS: the closed 6x6 agrees with the independent machinery to 1.3e-15 — the reduction is exact.

LA3_stationarity.verdict: the stationarity system P = dP/dc = dP/dy = 0 of the line-atom cubic solved to 90 digits: lambda* = 1.6310919765642504414737578928... (D(2) = sqrt(lambda*) = 1.2771421129...), c* = 0.397107287..., y* = 0.6563224670...: the optimum is an exact algebraic point of the explicit cubic system. The minimal polynomial of lambda* is the remaining open computation: the naive resultant elimination explodes (degree 1154 with extraneous components; artifacts saved: minpoly_r2v3.txt) and the in-sandbox LLL relation search did not converge in the time budget — external factoring (PARI/FLINT) of the saved system is the natural route.
